This proposed AD was prompted by a report of the loss of the tightening torque between the upper ball bearing end and a main rotor (MR) servo-control. This proposed AD would require an inspection of the nut tightening torque of the upper ball bearing end of all the MR servo-controls and, depending on the results, corrective actions. The proposed AD would also require reporting the inspection results. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21384","title":"Sunshine Act Meeting","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21384/sunshine-act-meeting","summary":"","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21383","title":"New Source Performance Standards and National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants; Delegation of Authority to Northwest Clean Air Agency, Washington State","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21383/new-source-performance-standards-and-national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants","summary":"The Northwest Clean Air Agency (NWCAA), located in Washington State, submitted updated regulations for receiving delegation and approval of its program for the implementation and enforcement of newly issued or revised New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) and National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAP), as provided for under previously approved delegation mechanisms. The updated regulations incorporate by reference certain NSPS and NESHAP promulgated by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) as they existed through October 18, 2023. The EPA is providing notice that it is proposing to update the delegation of certain NSPS and approve the delegation of certain NESHAP to NWCAA. The proposed delegation of authority under this action does not apply to sources located in Indian country.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21381","title":"Privacy Act of 1974; System of Records","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21381/privacy-act-of-1974-system-of-records","summary":"The Federal Communications Commission (FCC, Commission, or Agency) is modifying an existing system of records, FCC/WCB-1, Lifeline Program, subject to the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended. This action is necessary to meet the requirements of the Privacy Act to publish in the Federal Register notice of the existence and character of records maintained by the agency. The Lifeline Program (or \"Lifeline\") provides discounts for one Lifeline Program voice service per household and/or broadband internet access service (BIAS) to qualifying low- income individuals. Individuals may qualify for Lifeline through proof of income or participation in another qualifying program. Since the enactment of the Telecommunications Act of 1996 (1996 Act), the Lifeline Program has been administered by the Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC) under the direction of the Commission and, by delegation, of the Commission's Wireline Competition Bureau (WCB). This system of records contains information about individuals who have started an application online or applied to participate in the Lifeline Program, respondents to consumer surveys related to the Lifeline program, and enrollment representatives. The public is invited to submit comments on these requests.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21372","title":"President's Military Spouse Commission; Notice of Federal Advisory Committee Meeting","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21372/presidents-military-spouse-commission-notice-of-federal-advisory-committee-meeting","summary":"The DoD (referred to herein as \"Department of War\") is publishing this notice to announce that the following Federal Advisory Committee meeting of the President's Military Spouse Commission will take place.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21371","title":"Marine Mammals; Incidental Take of Polar Bears and Pacific Walruses in the Beaufort Sea and North Slope of Alaska","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21371/marine-mammals-incidental-take-of-polar-bears-and-pacific-walruses-in-the-beaufort-sea-and-north","summary":"We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), in response to a request under the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA) of 1972 from the Alaska Oil and Gas Association (AOGA), finalize regulations facilitating the authorization of incidental, unintentional take of small numbers of polar bears (Ursus maritimus) and Pacific walruses (Odobenus rosmarus divergens) during year-round oil and gas industry activities in the Beaufort Sea (Alaska and the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS)) and adjacent northern coast of Alaska. Take may result from oil and gas exploration, development, production, and transportation activities occurring for a period of 5 years. Oil and gas industry operations include similar types of activities covered by the previous 5-year Beaufort Sea incidental take regulations effective from August 6, 2021, through August 5, 2026. We will issue letters of authorization, upon request, for specific activities in accordance with these regulations.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21370","title":"Importer of Controlled Substances Application: Organic Standards Solutions International, LLC","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21370/importer-of-controlled-substances-application-organic-standards-solutions-international-llc","summary":"Organic Standards Solutions International, LLC has applied to be registered as an importer of basic class(es) of controlled substance(s).
